title: Lanuza pili: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Lanuza pili: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Lanuza pili is a pili variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Lanuza is a registered pili variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2000 as NSIC 2000 Pl 04.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Lanuza pili is grown

blocks.text: Compare it with the others in our [pili variety finder](/crop-varieties/pili), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Lanuza was about 19 years old and about 7 meters tall when it was registered. It bears every year, with fruit in year round. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.
A fruit of Lanuza weighs about 36.52 grams, and its shape is short oblong. The flesh is dark puple to black. Its fruiting season is year round, bearing annual.
Where and when to plant Lanuza pili

Bicol grows most of the pili. Pick a registered selection by kernel weight and the share of kernel in the nut, and plant grafted trees, because seedlings can turn out male. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Lanuza?
